kept.title: Unsafe Dynamic Code Execution (New Function)
kept.description: The router uses the `new Function()` constructor to build optimized routing functions based on user-defined constraints and handler patterns. In `lib/handler-storage.js` line 171 and 78, these functions are constructed using strings concatenated with potentially unsanitized inputs, creating a code injection vulnerability.
steps_to_exploit: Find a way to influence the constraints or parameter naming during router initialization.
Inject malicious JavaScript payloads into the constraint name or parameter name.
The router will incorporate these strings into the dynamically generated function body.
Trigger a route lookup, which will execute the injected code in the application context.
kept.impact: Full Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the server process.

kept.title: Regex Denial of Service (ReDoS) via Unsafe User-Provided Regex
kept.description: The router allows users to define custom regex parameters. While there is an `isRegexSafe` check, if `allowUnsafeRegex` is enabled, the system is susceptible to ReDoS during path matching, particularly in `index.js` at line 675.
steps_to_exploit: Set `allowUnsafeRegex: true` in the Router configuration.
Register a route with a complex, nested regex parameter that is vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking.
Send a specially crafted request path that forces the regex engine into exponential backtracking.
The CPU will hit 100% usage, effectively blocking other requests.
kept.impact: Denial of Service due to CPU exhaustion.

kept.title: Arbitrary Prototype Pollution in NullObject
kept.description: Although `NullObject` attempts to use `Object.create(null)` to prevent prototype pollution, the way params are assigned to the created object in `lib/handler-storage.js` (line 71) without checking for `__proto__` or `constructor` allows attackers to overwrite object properties.
steps_to_exploit: Identify a route that allows parameterized input.
Pass parameters that include reserved keys like `__proto__` or `constructor`.
The assignment in `lib/handler-storage.js` will attempt to set these properties, potentially polluting the object prototype if the context allows.
Trigger secondary logic that relies on these prototype-polluted objects.
kept.impact: Potential for application-wide logic bypass or data corruption.

kept.title: Information Leakage via Pretty Print
kept.description: The `prettyPrint` function in `lib/pretty-print.js` (line 165) exposes route information, including constraints and potentially sensitive metadata, to anyone who calls the function. If this endpoint is exposed publicly, it leaks the internal routing structure.
steps_to_exploit: Identify an endpoint that triggers `router.prettyPrint()`.
Make an authenticated or unauthenticated call to that endpoint.
Capture the returned output containing internal routing logic, constraints, and potentially user-defined metadata.
kept.impact: Exposure of internal API structure and sensitive configuration logic.

kept.title: Path Traversal via Improperly Sanitized URL
kept.description: The `safeDecodeURI` function in `lib/url-sanitizer.js` (line 46) attempts to decode URI components, but its handling of double-encoded characters and reserved delimiters can be bypassed, leading to potential path traversal or unexpected route matching.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a URL with double-encoded path segments or unexpected delimiters (like `;`).
Observe if the `safeDecodeURI` logic fails to normalize the path correctly.
Send a request that matches a route pattern incorrectly due to incomplete sanitization.
kept.impact: Security bypasses where restricted routes become accessible through path manipulation.

kept.title: Excessive Resource Consumption via Unbounded Route Parameter Length
kept.description: While `maxParamLength` is configurable, it defaults to 100 in `index.js` (line 98). If this is not strictly enforced by the user and configured effectively, large path parameters can cause excessive memory consumption when generating the param objects.
steps_to_exploit: Find a route with a catch-all or parametric segment.
Send a request with a massive path segment (e.g., millions of characters).
The memory allocation required to process these parameters in `index.js` might cause an OOM event.
kept.impact: Denial of Service via memory exhaustion.

kept.title: Potential Logic Bypass in Constraint Matching
kept.description: The `_buildConstraintStore` method in `lib/handler-storage.js` (line 88) uses bitmasks to identify matching routes. With a limit of 31 routes per node (line 51), there is a risk that complex constraint logic could be misinterpreted if the bitwise operations are not handled with perfect precision across different constraints.
steps_to_exploit: Create a node with exactly 31 routes and overlapping constraints.
Send requests that should match specific routes but might collide with others due to the bitmask logic.
Observe if a request is routed to the wrong handler.
kept.impact: Authorization or routing bypass resulting in incorrect handler execution.

kept.title: Insecure Default Configuration for Regex Matching
kept.description: The `allowUnsafeRegex` option defaults to `false` but can be globally toggled, and the default router initialization in `index.js` (line 100) exposes this configuration. Improperly handled, developers might enable it, creating ReDoS vectors.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker identifies an environment where `allowUnsafeRegex` has been set to `true`.
Submit complex regex inputs to the vulnerable route.
Trigger ReDoS.

kept.title: Weak Type Enforcement in Constraints
kept.description: The constraint system validates inputs using `validate()` methods, but in `lib/constrainer.js` (line 101), if a strategy is missing or not properly validated for a specific input, the router may behave unpredictably.
steps_to_exploit: Provide unexpected data types to a constraint field that doesn't explicitly enforce strict type checks.
Trigger the `newStoreForConstraint` function to handle unexpected state.
kept.impact: Unexpected application state or potential runtime errors.

kept.title: Lack of Deep Protection Against Prototype Pollution in `deepEqual`
kept.description: The use of `fast-deep-equal` in `index.js` (line 31) for route matching is generally safe, but if the comparison logic is used against user-supplied objects in `off()` or `on()`, an attacker might provide a payload that interacts with object internals.
steps_to_exploit: Send a request that forces `deepEqual` to compare a crafted user object against a system route object.
If the engine is vulnerable, this could lead to unexpected results or crashes.
kept.impact: Denial of Service or logic manipulation.

kept.title: Uncaught Exceptions in URL Decoding
kept.description: While `safeDecodeURI` is wrapped in a try/catch, if an error happens in `safeDecodeURIComponent` (line 84 in `lib/url-sanitizer.js`), the application flow might result in returning a partial path or `null` which could be misused.
steps_to_exploit: Send malformed percent-encoded sequences that trigger an error within the decoder.
Analyze the response to check if the error is handled safely.
kept.impact: Potential for application instability or uncaught crashes.

kept.title: Complexity and Maintenance Risk of Bitwise Logic
kept.description: The use of bitwise operations for handler matching in `lib/handler-storage.js` (line 131) is highly complex and error-prone, significantly increasing the probability of future logic bugs during security-sensitive updates.
steps_to_exploit: Attempt to find edge cases where bitwise masks interact with high-bit positions incorrectly.
Exploit potential off-by-one errors in constraint masking.
kept.impact: Long-term maintainability issues leading to potential critical vulnerabilities.

kept.title: Use of `var`/dynamic assignment in `new Function` generation
kept.description: The generated function body in `lib/handler-storage.js` (line 65) creates code strings that are later executed. The lack of strict mode in the generated function could lead to variable leakage into the outer scope.
steps_to_exploit: Inject variables during route definition that conflict with internal logic of the generated function.
Attempt to cause an identifier collision.
Trigger logic errors in the matching function.

kept.title: Insecure GitHub Workflow Permissions
kept.description: The workflow `.github/workflows/node.js.yml` (line 62) provides write permissions to pull requests, which could be exploited by a compromised PR to modify repository contents.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a PR with a malicious payload that triggers the automated workflow.
Use the excessive permissions to overwrite sensitive files in the repository.
kept.impact: Compromise of the repository build process and supply chain.

kept.title: Potentially Insecure Regex in Router
kept.description: The `FULL_PATH_REGEXP` used in `index.js` (line 39) is complex. If this regex is not perfectly crafted, it might be susceptible to ReDoS when processing long, specially crafted URLs.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a long string with repeated characters that match parts of the regex but eventually fail to match the full string.
Measure execution time to confirm backtracking behavior.
